title: Kinetic Energy
seo_title: Grade 8 Kinetic Energy Worksheets: KE = ½mv², Mass, Speed and Graphs
standard_text: Construct and interpret graphical displays of data to describe the relationships of kinetic energy to the mass of an object and to the speed of an object.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on kinetic energy (NGSS MS-PS3-1): KE = ½mv², how mass and speed affect kinetic energy, and reading graphs of kinetic energy data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_sub: Doubling the mass doubles kinetic energy. Doubling the speed makes it four times as large.
body_html:
How to think about it

Kinetic energy (KE) is the energy of motion. It depends on mass and speed:

KE = ½ × m × v² (m in kg, v in m/s, KE in joules)

  • Double the mass → KE doubles (straight-line graph).
  • Double the speed → KE becomes 4 times as large (graph curves upward).
Example

A 4 kg cart moves at 3 m/s. What is its KE?

½ × 4 × 3²

½ × 4 × 9

Answer: 18 J

Example

A bike has 200 J of KE. Its speed doubles. New KE?

2² = 4

4 × 200

Answer: 800 J

Common mistakes

  • Thinking doubling speed doubles KE. It makes it 4 times.
  • Forgetting the ½ or forgetting to square the speed.
  • Thinking an object at rest has kinetic energy.

faq.q: How do you calculate kinetic energy?
faq.a: KE = ½ × m × v², with mass in kilograms and speed in meters per second. The answer is in joules.

faq.q: Why does speed matter more than mass for kinetic energy?
faq.a: Speed is squared. Doubling speed gives 4 times the kinetic energy, but doubling mass only doubles it.

faq.q: What does a graph of kinetic energy vs. speed look like?
faq.a: It curves upward, because kinetic energy depends on the square of speed. A graph of KE vs. mass is a straight line.

items.q: What unit is used for energy?
items.e: 1 J = 1 kg·m²/s².

items.q: What is kinetic energy?
c: the energy an object has because it is moving
energy stored in an object's position
items.e: Moving objects have KE.

items.q: Nora measures a bicycle and rider with a mass of 80 kg moving at 6 m/s. What is its kinetic energy? (KE = ½ × m × v²)
Ruby measures a toy car with a mass of 3 kg moving at 5 m/s. What is its kinetic energy? (KE = ½ × m × v²)
If two balls roll at the same speed, which has more kinetic energy?
items.e: More mass → more KE.

items.q: Luis measures a bowling ball with a mass of 6 kg moving at 5 m/s. What is its kinetic energy? (KE = ½ × m × v²)
Why is a speeding truck more dangerous than a slow one?
c: Its kinetic energy is much larger, so a crash transfers much more energy.
items.e: KE grows with v².

items.q: Does a parked car have kinetic energy?
c: No, because it is not moving.
items.e: Speed is 0, so KE is 0.
